Retrieval_System_Blueprint.description: Retriever catalog specifically optimized for LoCoMo dataset - very long-term conversational memory evaluation benchmark with persona-driven dialogues, temporal event graphs, and multi-session reasoning.

dataset_context.name: LoCoMo (Long-term Conversational Memory)
dataset_context.description: Very long-term conversational dialogues (300 turns, 9K tokens avg, up to 35 sessions) grounded in personas and temporal event graphs
key_challenges: Very long context (9K tokens per conversation)
Temporal and causal understanding across sessions
Persona consistency (each agent has detailed background)
Five reasoning types: single-hop, multi-hop, temporal, commonsense, adversarial

single_hop.example: What did Caroline say about the LGBTQ support group?

multi_hop.description: Requires synthesizing information from multiple sessions
multi_hop.example: How did Caroline's therapy journey progress over time?

temporal.description: Requires reasoning about time and event sequences
temporal.example: When did Melanie paint a sunrise? What happened after Caroline started medication?
temporal.critical_note: LoCoMo shows LLMs struggle most with temporal reasoning (73% below human performance)

commonsense.description: Requires integrating external knowledge with dialogue context
commonsense.example: What fields would Caroline be likely to pursue given her interests?

adversarial.description: Designed to mislead the agent (test for hallucinations)
adversarial.example: Did Caroline ever mention going to Europe? (when she didn't)
adversarial.critical_note: Long-context LLMs show significant hallucinations on adversarial queries

metadata_available: speaker (persona names like Caroline, Melanie, Nate, Joanna)
persona (detailed background: age, occupation, relationships, interests)

ensemble.description: Hybrid fusion of FAISS (semantic) + BM25 (keyword) using Reciprocal Rank Fusion. BEST GENERAL-PURPOSE RETRIEVER for LoCoMo.
strengths: Handles LoCoMo's mixed query types (temporal + semantic + keyword)
Balances exact name matching (BM25) with conceptual understanding (FAISS)
Most robust for temporal queries: 'When did [person] [action]?'
Works across single-hop and multi-hop queries
Empirically proven effective in RAG systems for LoCoMo benchmark
weaknesses: Higher computational cost (runs two retrievers)
Still struggles with long-range temporal connections without explicit metadata filtering

success: When did Caroline go to the LGBTQ support group? → Finds 'Caroline' (keyword) + 'LGBTQ support group' (semantic) + temporal context
When did Melanie paint a sunrise? → Combines 'Melanie' (keyword) + 'paint' + 'sunrise' (semantic)
What medication did Caroline start? → Keyword 'medication' + semantic 'start' + speaker 'Caroline'
failure: Multi-session causal chains (e.g., 'How did X's situation evolve after Y happened 3 sessions ago?') - needs parent_document or better temporal scoring

ensemble.locomo_performance: Best overall retriever for LoCoMo temporal queries based on benchmark results showing RAG effectiveness
ensemble.recommendation: USE AS DEFAULT for temporal, single-hop, and mixed queries in LoCoMo

bm25.description: Keyword-based (Okapi BM25) lexical search. Excellent for exact name/term matches in LoCoMo personas.
strengths: Perfect for finding exact persona names (Caroline, Melanie, Nate, Joanna)
Excellent for unique keywords (LGBTQ, medication names, specific activities like 'painting', 'therapy')
Fast and computationally cheap
Ideal for single-hop factoid queries: 'What did [person] say about [specific_topic]?'
Handles adversarial queries well (checks for exact mentions to avoid hallucinations)
weaknesses: NO temporal understanding (critical weakness for LoCoMo)
Misses paraphrased or synonymous content
Cannot capture multi-hop reasoning across sessions
Doesn't understand persona consistency or event graph connections

success: What did Caroline say about therapy? → Exact keyword match for 'Caroline' + 'therapy'
Did Melanie mention painting? → Finds exact 'painting' mentions
What is Caroline's identity? (if explicitly stated) → Keyword match for 'identity' + 'Caroline'
failure: When did she go? → No temporal understanding of 'when'
What fields would Caroline pursue? → Misses conceptual inference about education/career
How did their friendship evolve? → Cannot trace multi-session progression

bm25.locomo_performance: Strong for single-hop factoid but FAILS on temporal reasoning (LoCoMo's hardest category)
bm25.recommendation: Use ONLY for single-hop factoid queries with explicit keywords; combine with ensemble for temporal queries

faiss.description: Dense semantic vector search using sentence embeddings. Best for conceptual/commonsense queries in LoCoMo.
strengths: Understands LoCoMo's natural language intent ('What happened when...', 'Why did...', 'How did...')
Captures semantic relationships between persona events
Excellent for commonsense reasoning: 'What fields would X pursue?' type queries
Handles paraphrased questions well
Good for identity/relationship queries when not explicitly stated
weaknesses: May miss exact persona names if semantically distant
No explicit temporal reasoning (like BM25)
Embedding space may not capture rare proper nouns well
Doesn't prioritize by session recency or temporal order

success: What fields would Caroline be likely to pursue? → Semantic understanding of education/career/interests
What is Caroline's identity? → Captures identity concepts even if not explicitly stated
Why did Caroline start therapy? → Understands causal reasoning semantically
failure: When did Caroline go to the LGBTQ support group? → No temporal prioritization
May retrieve wrong Caroline if multiple speakers with same name in different conversations

faiss.locomo_performance: Strong for commonsense reasoning (LoCoMo's conceptual queries)
faiss.recommendation: Use for commonsense/conceptual queries; combine with ensemble for temporal queries

parent_document.description: Retrieves entire session context for matched utterances. CRITICAL for LoCoMo's multi-hop and multi-session reasoning.
strengths: Provides full conversation session around the answer (solves LoCoMo's context fragmentation)
CRITICAL for multi-hop queries requiring information synthesis across turns
Captures event graph connections within sessions
Excellent for 'What was discussed in the session about X?' queries
Addresses 'lost in the middle' problem for long LoCoMo conversations
Provides persona consistency context across dialogue turns
weaknesses: Returns large text blocks (entire sessions - avg 300 tokens/session)
Overkill for simple single-hop factoid queries
Slower due to larger document processing
May exceed LLM context window if retrieving too many sessions

success: How did Caroline's therapy journey progress over time? → Returns full sessions showing progression
What was the conversation about when Caroline mentioned her identity? → Full session provides context
Describe the evolution of their friendship → Multiple full sessions show relationship development
failure: When did Caroline go to the LGBTQ support group? → Too much context for simple factoid

parent_document.locomo_performance: ESSENTIAL for multi-hop reasoning (LoCoMo's second hardest category after temporal)
parent_document.recommendation: USE for multi-hop and multi-session queries; avoid for single-hop factoids

multiquery.description: LLM expands query into multiple variations. Excellent for LoCoMo's ambiguous/short queries and commonsense reasoning.
strengths: Handles short LoCoMo queries like 'Caroline's research', 'Melanie's art'
Generates multiple perspectives for ambiguous questions
EXCELLENT for commonsense reasoning (expands conceptual queries)
Increases recall for poorly worded queries
Helps with multi-hop by expanding into sub-questions
weaknesses: LLM dependency (latency + cost)
May generate irrelevant query variants
Can introduce noise if expansion is too broad
NOT ideal for precise temporal factoids (expansion may dilute temporal specificity)

success: Caroline's education → Expands to 'What did Caroline study?', 'Caroline's educational background', 'Fields Caroline pursued'
What fields would Caroline pursue? → Expands to include 'interests', 'career aspirations', 'educational goals'
Melanie's art → Expands to 'What did Melanie paint?', 'Melanie's artistic activities', 'Melanie's creative work'
failure: When did Caroline go to LGBTQ support group? → Expansion may dilute temporal precision ('When' → 'What about', 'Why did', etc.)

multiquery.locomo_performance: Strong for commonsense reasoning and exploratory queries
multiquery.recommendation: Use for commonsense/conceptual queries and ambiguous questions; avoid for temporal factoids

time_weighted.description: Prioritizes recent documents using temporal decay. Good for LoCoMo 'recent events' queries but needs full temporal implementation.
strengths: Naturally prioritizes recent sessions in LoCoMo (uses session_datetime)
Good for 'What did X do recently/lately?' queries
Considers temporal ordering of sessions
Helpful for queries about 'latest' or 'most recent' events
weaknesses: Current implementation is basic FAISS (NEEDS UPGRADE to full temporal scoring)
May deprioritize older but more relevant information
Temporal decay function needs tuning for LoCoMo's multi-session structure
Doesn't capture complex temporal relationships ('before', 'after', 'between')
Not effective for 'When did X happen?' queries (needs exact date retrieval, not recency)

success: What did Caroline do recently? → Returns most recent sessions first
What's the latest update on Melanie's art? → Prioritizes recent mentions
failure: When did Melanie paint a sunrise? → Needs exact date, not recency ranking
What happened before Caroline started therapy? → No 'before' temporal logic

time_weighted.locomo_performance: Limited effectiveness - LoCoMo temporal queries need exact dates, not recency
time_weighted.recommendation: Use ONLY for 'recent/latest' queries; NOT for 'when did X happen' factoids; NEEDS ENHANCEMENT for LoCoMo

mmr.description: Maximal Marginal Relevance - diversifies results to avoid redundancy. Excellent for LoCoMo's multi-session exploration.
strengths: Returns diverse utterances from different LoCoMo sessions (up to 35 sessions)
Avoids repetitive similar utterances across long conversations
EXCELLENT for exploratory queries: 'What topics did X discuss?', 'What activities did X do?'
Provides good coverage of multi-session conversations
Helps with multi-hop by providing diverse context
weaknesses: May exclude highly relevant duplicate information
Not ideal for precise temporal or single-hop factoid queries
Diversity may sacrifice precision for specific answers

success: What topics did Caroline discuss? → Returns diverse utterances from different sessions covering various topics
What activities did Melanie do? → Diverse results: painting, photography, travel, etc.
Describe Caroline and Melanie's conversations → Diverse sampling across sessions
failure: When did Caroline go to LGBTQ support group? → May miss the exact answer if similar to another high-ranked result
What medication did Caroline start? → Diversity may deprioritize the specific answer

mmr.locomo_performance: Strong for exploratory queries and multi-session coverage
mmr.recommendation: Use for exploratory/broad queries; avoid for precise factoids

contextual_compression.description: LLM extracts only relevant sentences from retrieved documents. Good for filtering verbose LoCoMo conversations but expensive.
strengths: Removes conversational fluff from LoCoMo's long dialogues (avg 9K tokens)
Returns precise answer-containing sentences
Reduces context size for downstream LLM processing (critical for LoCoMo's long contexts)
Good for adversarial queries (filters out irrelevant distractions)
weaknesses: HIGH LATENCY (LLM must process each document)
EXPENSIVE (LLM calls for large retrieval sets)
May accidentally remove useful surrounding context (persona details, temporal cues)
Risk of removing important context for multi-hop reasoning
Empirically, LoCoMo shows RAG with observations (assertions) outperforms compression

success: What medication did Caroline start? → From long conversation, extracts only: 'Caroline started taking metformin'
Did Caroline mention going to Europe? (adversarial) → Filters out all utterances, returns nothing (correct)
failure: How did Caroline's therapy journey progress? → May remove context like session transitions, temporal markers

contextual_compression.locomo_performance: Moderate - LoCoMo research shows observations-based RAG outperforms compression
contextual_compression.recommendation: Use sparingly for adversarial queries; prefer ensemble for most cases; HIGH COST

self_query.description: LLM parses query to extract metadata filters (speaker, date, session). POWERFUL but unavailable in current implementation.
self_query.locomo_ranking: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Potentially Best for Speaker/Temporal Filtering - IF AVAILABLE)
strengths: Automatically filters by speaker/persona (Caroline, Melanie, Nate, Joanna)
Can filter by temporal metadata if dates mentioned in query
Natural language metadata filtering: 'show me Caroline's messages from May 2023'
IDEAL for LoCoMo's rich metadata (speaker, session_datetime, session_id)
Would dramatically improve speaker-specific and temporal queries
weaknesses: CURRENTLY UNAVAILABLE (requires langchain_classic package)
Requires LLM (adds latency and cost)
Depends on LLM correctly parsing metadata intent
May misinterpret ambiguous metadata references

success: Show me what Caroline said in May 2023 → Filters to speaker='Caroline' AND session_datetime='May 2023'
What did Melanie discuss in her recent sessions? → speaker='Melanie' + recent sessions
failure: If LLM misparses 'Caroline' as topic instead of speaker filter

self_query.locomo_performance: POTENTIALLY BEST for speaker/temporal filtering - but UNAVAILABLE
self_query.recommendation: FALLBACK to ensemble or bm25; IMPLEMENT if possible for LoCoMo

tfidf.description: Traditional TF-IDF information retrieval. Similar to BM25 but simpler scoring.
strengths: Fast keyword matching
Good for exact term lookups
Works well with unique terms in LoCoMo personas
weaknesses: Less sophisticated than BM25 for LoCoMo use cases
No semantic understanding
No temporal reasoning
Generally outperformed by BM25 or ensemble for all LoCoMo query types

success: Find 'sunrise painting' → Exact matches of 'sunrise' and 'painting'
failure: Same weaknesses as BM25 but less effective across the board

tfidf.locomo_performance: Weak - use BM25 or ensemble instead
tfidf.recommendation: AVOID in production; use BM25 or ensemble instead

svm.description: Support Vector Machine based ranking using embeddings. ML approach for LoCoMo retrieval.
strengths: Could learn LoCoMo-specific patterns if trained on the benchmark
Uses embeddings like FAISS but with ML ranking
Potential to capture complex patterns in persona consistency and event graphs
weaknesses: Requires training data (LoCoMo QA annotations could be used)
More complex than semantic search
Without fine-tuning, similar performance to FAISS
No temporal understanding
svm.locomo_performance: Experimental - similar to FAISS without training
svm.recommendation: Use FAISS instead; consider SVM only for research experiments

long_context_reorder.description: Reorders retrieved documents for optimal LLM processing. USEFUL for LoCoMo RAG pipeline with long contexts.
strengths: Puts most relevant context at beginning/end (LLM attention sweet spots)
Reduces 'lost in the middle' problem for LoCoMo's long conversations (9K tokens)
Improves RAG answer quality for multi-session contexts
Empirically shown to improve long-context LLM performance
weaknesses: Post-processing step, NOT primary retrieval
Assumes LLM attention patterns (may vary by model)
Minimal impact for small context windows
Doesn't fix poor initial retrieval

success: Any LoCoMo query with RAG where multiple sessions are retrieved → Reorders to put most relevant at start/end
failure: Doesn't fix poor retrieval (e.g., if relevant sessions not retrieved)

long_context_reorder.locomo_performance: Helpful for RAG with long LoCoMo contexts
long_context_reorder.recommendation: Use as POST-PROCESSING after ensemble/parent_document retrieval for multi-session contexts

LoCoMo_Orchestrator_Decision_Tree.description: Optimized decision logic for selecting retrievers based on LoCoMo query characteristics

rules.condition: Query is TEMPORAL ('When did', 'What date', 'What time')
rules.reasoning: LoCoMo's hardest category (73% below human performance). Needs keyword + semantic + temporal metadata.

rules.condition: Query is MULTI-HOP ('How did X progress', 'Describe evolution', 'What happened after')
rules.reasoning: Requires full session context and information synthesis across turns.

rules.condition: Query is SPEAKER-SPECIFIC with person name ('What did [Caroline/Melanie] say/do')
rules.reasoning: Need exact name matching + semantic understanding.

rules.condition: Query is COMMONSENSE/CONCEPTUAL ('What fields would X pursue', 'Why did X')
rules.reasoning: Requires semantic understanding and inference, not just keyword matching.

rules.condition: Query is ADVERSARIAL (asking about non-existent events)
rules.reasoning: Need precise keyword matching to verify mentions and avoid hallucinations.

rules.condition: Query is EXPLORATORY ('What topics did X discuss', 'Describe their conversations')
rules.reasoning: Need diverse results from multiple sessions.
Need query expansion to capture intent.

rules.condition: Query is IDENTITY/RELATIONSHIP ('Who is X', 'What is X's identity', 'Describe X')
rules.reasoning: Need semantic understanding of identity concepts, possibly with full context.

rules.condition: Query is RECENT/LATEST ('What did X do recently', 'latest update')
Query is SINGLE-HOP FACTOID with clear keywords
rules.reasoning: Simple factoid lookup with exact terms.
Ensemble is most robust for mixed or unclear queries in LoCoMo.

temporal_queries.critical_notes: MOST IMPORTANT: LoCoMo shows LLMs struggle most with temporal reasoning. Use ensemble for hybrid approach. Temporal decay (time_weighted) NOT effective for exact dates.
examples: When did Caroline go to the LGBTQ support group? → ensemble
When did Melanie paint a sunrise? → ensemble
What date did Caroline start therapy? → ensemble

multi_hop_queries.critical_notes: Need full session context for multi-turn reasoning. Parent_document returns entire sessions (avg 300 tokens/session).
examples: How did Caroline's therapy journey progress over time? → parent_document
What happened after Caroline started medication? → parent_document
Describe the evolution of their friendship → parent_document + mmr

speaker_specific_queries.critical_notes: Need exact persona name matching (Caroline, Melanie, Nate, Joanna). BM25 for keywords, ensemble for robustness.
examples: What did Caroline say about therapy? → ensemble
What did Melanie paint? → bm25 or ensemble
What research did Caroline do? → ensemble

commonsense_reasoning_queries.critical_notes: LoCoMo tests commonsense integration with dialogue context. FAISS for semantic understanding, multiquery for expansion.
examples: What fields would Caroline be likely to pursue in her education? → faiss
Why did Caroline start therapy? → faiss or ensemble
What career might Melanie pursue given her interests? → multiquery + faiss

adversarial_queries.critical_notes: CRITICAL: Long-context LLMs show significant hallucinations on adversarial LoCoMo queries. Need exact keyword matching to verify mentions.
examples: Did Caroline ever mention going to Europe? (she didn't) → bm25
Did Melanie discuss quantum physics? (she didn't) → bm25

exploratory_queries.critical_notes: MMR provides diversity across LoCoMo's multi-session structure (up to 35 sessions).
examples: What topics did Caroline and Melanie discuss? → mmr
What activities did Melanie do? → mmr
Describe their friendship → mmr + parent_document

patterns: What is X's relationship to Y
identity_relationship_queries.critical_notes: Identity often not explicitly stated. Need semantic understanding + surrounding context.
examples: What is Caroline's identity? → faiss
Who is Caroline? → faiss or parent_document
Describe Melanie's background → parent_document

patterns: What did X say about Y
single_hop_factoid_queries.critical_notes: Simplest LoCoMo category. BM25 sufficient if keywords clear, ensemble for safety.
examples: What medication did Caroline start? → bm25 or ensemble
What did Caroline say about LGBTQ support group? → bm25

recent_latest_queries.critical_notes: Time_weighted prioritizes recent sessions. NOT for 'when did X happen' (use ensemble).
examples: What did Caroline do recently? → time_weighted
What's the latest update on Melanie's art? → time_weighted

short_ambiguous_queries.critical_notes: Multiquery expands short queries into multiple variations for better coverage.
examples: Caroline's education → multiquery
Melanie's art → multiquery
therapy → multiquery + ensemble

temporal_reasoning_critical.problem: LoCoMo benchmark shows temporal reasoning is HARDEST (73% below human performance)
temporal_reasoning_critical.solution: ALWAYS use ensemble for temporal queries. Combine keyword matching (person/event) with semantic understanding (when/date context). DO NOT use time_weighted for 'when did X happen' queries (it's for recency, not exact dates).

multi_hop_requires_context.problem: Multi-hop queries need information synthesis across sessions
multi_hop_requires_context.solution: Use parent_document to retrieve entire sessions (provides full context). Combine with MMR for diverse session coverage. Avoid single-utterance retrieval.

adversarial_avoid_hallucinations.problem: Long-context LLMs hallucinate on adversarial LoCoMo queries
adversarial_avoid_hallucinations.solution: Use BM25 for exact keyword verification. If query asks 'Did X mention Y?', use BM25 to check for exact 'Y' mentions. Empty results = didn't mention.

commonsense_needs_semantics.problem: Commonsense queries require inference beyond keywords
commonsense_needs_semantics.solution: Use FAISS for semantic understanding. Combine with multiquery to expand conceptual queries into multiple perspectives.

default_to_ensemble.solution: Ensemble is most robust hybrid approach for LoCoMo. Combines BM25 (keywords) + FAISS (semantics). Safe default.

avoid_tfidf_svm.problem: TFIDF and SVM underperform in LoCoMo
avoid_tfidf_svm.solution: Use BM25 instead of TFIDF. Use FAISS instead of SVM. Only use for baseline comparisons.

contextual_compression_expensive.problem: Contextual compression has high latency/cost for LoCoMo's long contexts
contextual_compression_expensive.solution: LoCoMo research shows observations-based RAG outperforms compression. Use compression sparingly, only for adversarial filtering.

self_query_unavailable.problem: Self-query is BEST for speaker/temporal filtering but unavailable
self_query_unavailable.solution: Fallback to ensemble or BM25 for speaker-specific queries. Consider implementing self_query for production LoCoMo systems.

LoCoMo_Retriever_Rankings.description: Overall effectiveness ranking for LoCoMo dataset based on benchmark analysis

tier_1_essential.reasoning: Ensemble handles LoCoMo's hardest categories (temporal + mixed queries). Parent_document essential for multi-hop reasoning.

tier_2_specialized.reasoning: Strong for specific query types: FAISS (commonsense), BM25 (factoids), multiquery (ambiguous), MMR (exploratory).

tier_3_supporting.reasoning: Supporting roles: time_weighted (recent queries), compression (filtering), reorder (post-processing).

tier_4_avoid.reasoning: Outperformed by tier 1-2 retrievers. Use only for baselines.

tier_unavailable.reasoning: Would be tier 1 (best for speaker/temporal filtering) but currently unavailable. IMPLEMENT if possible.

critical_instructions: 1. ALWAYS check if query is temporal ('When', 'What date') → MUST use ensemble (LoCoMo's hardest category)
2. ALWAYS check if query is multi-hop ('How did X progress', 'What happened after') → MUST use parent_document
3. ALWAYS check for speaker names (Caroline, Melanie, Nate, Joanna) → prefer ensemble or bm25
4. ALWAYS check for commonsense/conceptual ('What fields', 'Why', 'likely') → prefer faiss or multiquery
5. ALWAYS check for adversarial (asking about non-existent events) → prefer bm25 for verification
7. NEVER use time_weighted for 'when did X happen' queries (use ensemble)
8. NEVER use tfidf or svm in production (use bm25 or faiss instead)
9. DEFAULT to ensemble if query type unclear (safest hybrid approach)
10. CONSIDER long_context_reorder as post-processing for multi-session retrieval

key_findings: LoCoMo is the first very long-term conversational memory benchmark (300 turns, 9K tokens, up to 35 sessions)
Temporal reasoning is hardest for LLMs (73% below human performance)
Long-context LLMs (GPT-4, Gemini) show significant hallucinations on adversarial queries
RAG with observations (short assertions) outperforms other RAG strategies including compression
Multi-hop reasoning requires full session context, not just single utterances
Persona consistency and event graph grounding are critical for realistic memory evaluation
rag_strategy_recommendations: Use observations-based RAG (extract assertions) rather than full document RAG
Combine retrieval with temporal/causal reasoning modules
Filter adversarial queries with exact keyword matching (BM25)
Use full session context (parent_document) for multi-hop queries
Reorder long contexts to avoid 'lost in the middle' problem
Research_Insights_from_LoCoMo_Paper.citation: Maharana et al. (2024). LoCoMo: Very Long-Term Conversational Memory. Snap Research.
